metas.name: Amazonas 8B
metas.note: Road 8B is a thin paved road (divided north of Chachapoyas) surrounded by distinct looking mountains. South towards the Cajamarca border the road runs along the edge of the mountain.

metas.name: Amazonas Mountains
metas.note: Mountains in this region are covered in green vegetation but have very visible rocky outcrops that give it a rugged appearance. These mountains are visible in most of the region.

metas.name: Amazonas/Cajamarca Valley
metas.note: Near Bagua and Jaén, there’s a large open valley with surrounding hills featuring rice fields and palm trees. It may look a bit like the area near Tarapoto, but the mountains look different and the area is drier.

metas.name: Ancash 106
metas.note: Road 106 is a gen 4 dirt road in the Cordillera Blanca and is one of the most beautiful and easily recognizable roads in Peru.

metas.name: Ancash 1N Landscape
metas.note: Road 1N in Ancash (and parts of Lima) passes through a sandy desert landscape. A divided highway through desert with sand dunes is a good indicator of Ancash region.

metas.name: Ancash Cordillera Blanca Mountain Range
metas.note: Most of Peru’s snow-capped mountains are in the Cordillera Blanca mountain range in Ancash region, which also includes Peru’s highest peak, Nevado Huascarán.

metas.name: Ancash Foggy Roads
metas.note: Very foggy roads can be found in Ancash region, in the mountains west of Yungay.

metas.name: Ancash Gen 4 Landscape
metas.note: Ancash region has hilly landscapes with lots of eucalyptus trees.

metas.name: Ancash Mountains Roads
metas.note: Landscapes with big, rugged mountain peaks (some covered by snow) can be found in the Cordillera Blanca mountain range in Ancash.

metas.name: Ancash/LaLibertad Border Road
metas.note: The Ancash/La Libertad border road passes through dry, rocky mountains. Most of the road looks like this. While part of it is two lanes, the majority is a narrow, paved road.

metas.name: Apurimac 30A
metas.note: Road 30A cuts through a gorge. The entire road has overcast coverage, giving it a slightly dark appearance. The mountains are very recognizable.

metas.name: Apurimac 30B
metas.note: Road 30B is a thin, paved road with distinct-looking pavement, having darker lines a bit like Texas pavement.

metas.name: Apurimac Abancay Town
metas.note: The town of Abancay is surrounded by tall, brown mountains with sparse vegetation, visible from most parts of the city.

metas.name: Apurimac Gen 3 Landscape
metas.note: The gen 3 coverage near Andahuaylas is tricky. The landscape looks lush, similar to Cajamarca. The combination of very overcast skies, black gen 3 car, and tall eucalyptus trees is a good clue for this area.

metas.name: Apurimac Main Road 3S
metas.note: Road 3S in Apurimac, the main road between Ayacucho and Cusco, is a winding route along the edge of the mountains. Its elevated position overlooking a valley is a good indicator of Apurimac region.

metas.name: Arequipa 1S Highway
metas.note: The 1S coastal highway in Arequipa region is a non-divided road that runs along the ocean and sometimes has a blur on one side of the image.

metas.name: Arequipa Camana/Punta de Bombon
metas.note: Agricultural fields surrounded by sand dunes on all sides except south can be found at the cities of Camana and Punta de Bombon.

metas.name: Arequipa Central Valley
metas.note: In central Arequipa region, at the cities of Majes and La Joya, there is a flat valley with small mountains in the distance. The valley has a lot of agriculture including prickly pear cacti fields.

metas.name: Arequipa Coastal Valleys
metas.note: Coastal valleys with dry, vegetation-free mountains are most common in Arequipa region. These mountains often appear smoother and lighter in color than those in northern coastal regions of Peru.

metas.name: Arequipa Colca Canyon
metas.note: The area near Chivay features the Colca Canyon along with snowcapped mountains and terrace-farmed agricultural fields.

metas.name: Arequipa Town
metas.note: Arequipa has a distinctive colonial-style architecture, with arched windows and small overhanging roofs. Many houses in the old-town are built from sillar, a white volcanic rock. This cobblestone pavement is also quite common in the city.

metas.name: Arequipa Volcanoes
metas.note: Arequipa’s volcanoes, Misti and Chachani, are visible from much of the surrounding area.

metas.name: Arequipa Walls
metas.note: These brickly looking walls out of white volcanic rock are a good clue for Arequipa region.

metas.name: Ayacucho 28B
metas.note: Road 28B in Ayacucho region looks similar to the one in Cusco as it passes through tropical hills, but this section has road lines, unlike the more recognizable part in Cusco region.

metas.name: Ayacucho 30A
metas.note: Road 30A, between Nazca and Puquio, is a winding road passing through rugged, dry mountain ranges. Also these bollards are common along this road.

metas.name: Ayacucho 30A South
metas.note: East of Puquio lies a vast, open plain of arid terrain. It is sparsely vegetated with low-lying brown and beige scrub. Much of the coverage is very overcast and appears a bit dark.

metas.name: Ayacucho 30D
metas.note: Road 30D through central Ayacucho is a thin, paved, high-elevation mountain road. The landscape is very barren, similar to roads in Huancavelica region.

metas.name: Ayacucho 32
metas.note: Road 32 near Puquio is a thin mountain road. The northern section is a dirt road, while the southern section is paved. It has some bushes and shrubs, also rock walls are common along this road.

metas.name: Cajamarca 5N North
metas.note: The main roads in northern Cajamarca, near the Ecuador border, are mountainous, and pass through tropical vegetation.

metas.name: Cajamarca Gen 3
metas.note: Cajamarca region has dense gen 3 dirt road coverage. Lush looking landscapes with lots of eucalyptus trees. Many houses have metal sheet roofs that reflect the sunlight. Often fields are fenced off by tree rows, similar to Ecuador and southern Colombia.

metas.name: Cajamarca Gen 4
metas.note: Cajamarca is hilly with lots of eucalyptus trees and more lush than regions in the south. Buildings often have overhanging roofs with wooden supports.

metas.name: Cajamarca High Elevation Steppe
metas.note: Cajamarca region at high elevation can have this unusual for the region looking grassland steppe with sparse vegetation.

metas.name: Cajamarca Jaen Offroads
metas.note: Tropical mountain roads, often dirt roads, passing through lush vegetation are common near Jaén and up to the Ecuador border. The hills are bigger than in other Amazonian regions such as San Martin.

metas.name: Cajamarca Pines
metas.note: Pine tree plantations are most common in Cajamarca region.

metas.name: Cajamarca Town
metas.note: Cajamarca city can be identified by its abundance of northern-style roofs (overhanging with wooden supports) and white colonial-style architecture.

metas.name: Cusco 113 Smallcam
metas.note: Cusco region has a few smallcam roads passing through the rainforest. Road 113, which leads to Manu National Park, is a narrow paved road surrounded by tropical vegetation.

metas.name: Cusco 28B
metas.note: The 28B is one of the most useful Amazonian roads to learn. The entire road runs along a river valley and has no road lines. Sections of the road are unpaved, but the majority is paved without road lines.

metas.name: Cusco 30C and Puno 34B
metas.note: These two roads descend through a valley of big tropical mountains. The roads are in good condition and have lots of bollards as well as yellow-black markings on guardrails. 34B drives north, 30C SW towards Cusco.

metas.name: Cusco Ausangate Mountain
metas.note: Recognizable mountain: Ausangate.

metas.name: Cusco City
metas.note: The town of Cusco has both red brick houses and white Spanish colonial-style buildings. It is surrounded by mountains. Buildings with orange or red tiled roofs are most common in Cusco region.

metas.name: Cusco East Landscape
metas.note: In southeastern Cusco, near the Puno border, there is a gradual transition between the rolling hills of the southern Altiplano and the slightly more forested landscapes of Cusco.

metas.name: Cusco Sacred Valley
metas.note: If you see steep, rugged brown mountains in a valley, you are probably in the Sacred Valley near Cusco, between Ollantaytambo and Pisac.

metas.name: Cusco South Gen 3
metas.note: This gen 3 coverage, with a white (or almost blurred-out) Google car, very overcast skies, and a wintery feel (often with snow on the mountaintops), is found in southern Cusco region between Sicuani and the Arequipa region border.

metas.name: Cusco South Landscape
metas.note: The far southern part of Cusco region has gen 4 roads across landscapes similar to Puno’s Altiplano. Some of the roads are wide without road lines, others are unpaved.

metas.name: Huancavelica Gen 4
metas.note: Most of Huancavelica region has high-elevation roads with rugged, barren mountains. Many of the roads are thin, paved mountain roads with white outside lines and no middle line. Almost entirely gen 4 2025.

metas.name: Huancavelica North/East Landscape
metas.note: Eastern and northern Huancavelica region has a different landscape, with river valleys that are at a lower elevation and have a bit more vegetation, like bushes and shrubs.

metas.name: Huanta Landscape
metas.note: Semi-urban landscapes with red soil dirt roads, some trees, prickly pear cacti, mud walls are common near the town of Huanta in northern Ayacucho region.

metas.name: Huanuco 14A
metas.note: Road 14A is a narrow, paved gen 4 road winding through hilly tropical vegetation.

metas.name: Huanuco 2024 Coverage
metas.note: Huanuco region has gen 4 2024 rainy season coverage with lush hills and landscapes.

metas.name: Huanuco Tingo Maria Landscape
metas.note: Near Tingo Maria, the landscape is tropical, with large hills completely covered by trees. This differs from the area near Tarapoto, which has smaller hills with some green grass patches.

metas.name: Huanuco Town
metas.note: The city of Huanuco is surrounded by huge dark-green, barren mountains.

metas.name: Huanuco Unfinished Roads
metas.note: Unfinished roads (paved roads without road lines) are common in Huanuco region.

metas.name: Ica Desert Roads
metas.note: Sandy gen 4 desert roads are most common in Ica region.

metas.name: Ica Nazca Bollard
metas.note: Rectangular concrete bollards like these are only found around Nazca.

metas.name: Ica sand dunes
metas.note: Sand dunes can occasionally be seen in the city of Ica.

metas.name: Ica tar lines
metas.note: Roads covered with black tar lines are most common in Ica region.

metas.name: Ica trees
metas.note: Small, dead-looking trees by the road are another good clue for identifying Ica region.

metas.name: Ica tuktuks
metas.note: Ica uses tuktuks with closed compartments, unlike the cities in northern coastal Peru (Lima has both types).

metas.name: Ica/Lima 2025 valleys
metas.note: Valleys featuring rugged, dry mountains and 2025 copyright are mostly in Ica and Lima regions.

metas.name: Junin Amazonian Roads
metas.note: The Amazonian part of Junin region is hilly and tropical. It’s mostly gen 4, with 22 (if 22 amazonian then always Junin), 23 or 26 copyright.

metas.name: Junin Huancayo
metas.note: Huancayo can be recognized by the huge mountains surrounding the city, as well as its grid.

metas.name: Junin Huancayo Valley
metas.note: The valley between Huancayo and Jauja is a flat plain with trees, agricultural areas, and villages. It runs at a NNW angle and is surrounded by mountains.

metas.name: Junin North Landscape
metas.note: Northern Junin, near Peru’s second-largest lake, has a more open landscape with rolling hills. This can look very similar to areas across the border in Pasco region.

metas.name: Junin/Pasco Landscape
metas.note: Junin and Pasco regions are located on the central high-altitude plateau, featuring grassy hills with almost no vegetation and exposed rock. Puno region can look similar, but it has less exposed rock.

metas.name: La Libertad Gen 3 Landscape
metas.note: Gen 3 hilly landscapes with lots of eucalyptus trees. Often dirt roads. The landscape can look similar to Cajamarca but it’s a bit less lush. Black gen 3 car is most common.

metas.name: La Libertad Landscape
metas.note: These light-brown, rugged mountains are more common in semi-coastal northern Peru, especially in La Libertad region. The valleys often have agricultural fields.

metas.name: La Libertad Sugar Cane
metas.note: Sugar cane fields stretch along the coast between Chiclayo and Lima, with the majority located between Chiclayo and Chimbote. Most are in La Libertad region.

metas.name: Lambayeque Coastal Landscape
metas.note: Flat landscapes with small canals and agriculture are most common near the city of Chiclayo.

metas.name: Lambayeque Hills
metas.note: Landscapes with some bushes, dry looking vegetation and scattered hills all around are mostly in Lambayeque region.

metas.name: Lima Gen 3 Landscape
metas.note: Gen 3 mountain dirt roads with dry, yellowish-brown grass and small shrubs/bushes are most common in Lima region. The sky is also often hazy. Gen 3 black car is most common.

metas.name: Lima Hills
metas.note: On the outskirts of Lima, you can find these dry-looking mountains, often with many poor neighborhoods built on them.

metas.name: Lima Town
metas.note: A good clue for Lima is overcast weather, as other coastal areas often have clear blue skies. Boulevard-type streets are also mostly only found in Lima.

metas.name: Lima/Ica Bollards
metas.note: These bollards are only found on the highway between Ica and Lima.

metas.name: Loreto Iquitos Road Pavement
metas.note: This dark asphalt pavement is almost on the entire road to Iquitos as well as in parts of the city, making it the easiest way to recognize the area. All roads in Iquitos are gen 3.

metas.name: Loreto Iquitos Rural Roads
metas.note: Iquitos has a few rural roads west of town with very sandy soil.

metas.name: Loreto Iquitos Town
metas.note: Roads inside Iquitos have both the dark asphalt found on the road to Iquitos and concrete pavement. Transitions between these pavement types are often in poor condition.

metas.name: Loreto South Iquitos Pavement
metas.note: The far southern section of the road to Iquitos has a different pavement than the rest of the road. It can also be slightly hilly.

metas.name: Loreto Yurimaguas Road
metas.note: The road to Yurimaguas is mostly flat and tropical. It looks similar to the road to Pucallpa.

metas.name: MDD 30C
metas.note: Road 30C is a flat, well paved road passing through the rain forest. It has clear skies, unlike most other Amazonian main roads. On the southern section, the sky has an orange tint.

metas.name: MDD 30C Offroads
metas.note: Gen 3 rainforest dirt roads are side roads off the 30C. If it's flat you are likely near Puerto Maldonado, if it's hilly you are closer to the Brazilian border.

metas.name: MDD Bollards
metas.note: These sticks are only found on the 30C.

metas.name: Moquegua 108
metas.note: Road 108 is a gen 4 dirt road with sparse arid vegetation, including shrubs, bushes, and some cacti. Snowcapped mountains may also be visible.

metas.name: Moquegua 36A Road
metas.note: Road 36A in Moquegua has an arid landscape with scattered bushes and shrubs. Similar-looking terrain can also be found in Tacna and in south-western Ayacucho regions.

metas.name: Moquegua Bollard
metas.note: This bollard can only be found in the region of Moquegua.

metas.name: Moquegua Ilo
metas.note: Moquegua’s second-largest city, Ilo, is a somewhat hilly coastal city surrounded by sand dunes.

metas.name: Moquegua Mountains
metas.note: The city of Moquegua is surrounded by rocky, light-colored, dry mountains. These mountains are also a good way to recognize Moquegua region.

metas.name: Moquegua North-East Landscape
metas.note: High-elevation, barren gen 4 desert roads with pale beige sand and almost no vegetation can be found in northeastern Moquegua, near the borders with Tacna and Puno.

metas.name: Moquegua Ruta 1
metas.note: The coastal highway in Moquegua region runs north-south along the ocean and is quite winding.

metas.name: Pasco 18 Pavement
metas.note: This unique concrete pavement exists only on Road 18 in Pasco and Lima regions.

metas.name: Pasco 5N Dirt Road
metas.note: The section of the 5N passing through the mountains in Pasco region is a winding, unpaved dirt road (c2023). The only other roads that may look similar are the unpaved sections of the 28B, but the 5N is generally more winding and narrow.

metas.name: Pasco Cerro de Pasco
metas.note: Cerro de Pasco is a very high-elevation mining town. The buildings have metal sheet roofs, and the town is surrounded by rugged, barren mountains.

metas.name: Pasco Lakes
metas.note: Lakes on a very open, high-elevation, hilly, and barren landscape can be found in western Pasco region.

metas.name: Pasco Landscape
metas.note: Most of Pasco region lies on the central high-elevation plateau. The landscapes are similar to northern Junin: grassy plains with rolling hills and distant mountains.

metas.name: Pasco North Landscape
metas.note: Northern Pasco looks different from the rest of the region, featuring valleys through hills covered with eucalyptus trees.

metas.name: Pasco North Mountains Landscape
metas.note: Northern Pasco also has some higher-elevation gen 3 roads on hilly terrain with little to no vegetation.

metas.name: Pasco Oxapampa
metas.note: Oxapampa features wooden elements reminiscent of architecture in the Alps (this type of architecture can only be found in Pasco and Junin). The town can also be recognized by the forested, tropical hills that surround it.

metas.name: Pasco/Huanuco 5N
metas.note: Road 5N towards Pucallpa in Pasco and Huanuco regions is a mostly straight, north-south, flat road in good condition surrounded by tropical vegetation. Use road angle to find the right stretch.

metas.name: Peru Chincha Agriculture
metas.note: Northern Ica region is greener, with most agriculture concentrated around the town of Chincha. This area is mostly overcast.

metas.name: Peru Ica South Desert
metas.note: Southern Ica region has a desert landscape, a lot of it has dark looking soil.

metas.name: Peru KM Marker
metas.note: KM markers that start with PE are national roads. If they have 2 different letters they are regional and those letters are an abbreviation for the region name. They will also have a different color than black.

metas.name: Peru Region Poles
metas.note: Poles in Peru occasionally have the region name (or an abbreviation for it) written on them.

metas.name: Peru South Bollard
metas.note: This bollard is generally more common in the southern half of the country.

metas.name: Peru South Desert
metas.note: Non-coastal, flat, gen 4 desert landscapes are mostly found on the roads between Tacna, Moquegua and Arequipa. Use road angle to find the right stretch. Tacna has more red soil.

metas.name: Piura 1N
metas.note: The eastern 1N road between Lambayeque and Piura regions runs straight NNW, with a significant mountain ridge to the east.

metas.name: Piura Coastal Gen 3 Landscapes
metas.note: Gen 3 landscapes with light grayish sandy soil and sparse vegetation are found near the coast in western Piura region.

metas.name: Piura East Dry Hills
metas.note: Eastern Piura region is hilly, with dry-looking trees and bushes. These arid hills are a good indicator for northern Peru.

metas.name: Piura East Landscape
metas.note: Eastern Piura looks similar to Cajamarca region: hilly terrain, many eucalyptus trees, lush vegetation, and houses with northern-style roofs. Many roads in Piura are unpaved. Political logos can also help differentiate the two regions.

metas.name: Piura NW Landscape
metas.note: Northwestern Piura has a similarly dry climate with sparse vegetation, but it is noticeably hillier, featuring rugged, eroded hills made of dry earth or sedimentary rock.

metas.name: Piura SW Landscape
metas.note: Most of Piura region has a very arid climate, with the only vegetation being scattered bushes and shrubs. Southwestern Piura is quite flat.

metas.name: Piura Town
metas.note: The towns of Piura and Sullana can most easily be recognized by the abbundance of these mesquite trees, which are less common in coastal regions south of it.

metas.name: Piura Trees
metas.note: Mesquite trees are very common in Piura region. They can also be found in Lambayeque, Tumbes, and Ica, but Piura has the highest abundance. Mesquite trees can also help identify Piura region in urban areas.

metas.name: Piura Valleys
metas.note: Near the town of Piura, there are a few valleys with some agriculture, though less than in regions south of Piura.

metas.name: Pole 1 Letter 4 Digits Horizontal
metas.note: Pole marking starting with an A followed by 4 digits are only found in Tumbes and Piura regions.

metas.name: Pole 6 Digits Vertical
metas.note: 6 digits vertical pole markings are common in Tumbes and Piura (can also be found in Lambayeque, Cajamarca and Tacna).

metas.name: Pole 7 Digits Vertical
metas.note: 7 digits vertical pole markings are common in Cajamarca, La Libertad and Ancash (rarely Piura, Lambayeque, Tacna). The code can start with 0 or another digit. If it's not 0 it tells you the region: 2 & 4 - Ancash; 3 - Cajamarca; 5 - La Libertad

metas.name: Pole 8 Digits Horizontal
metas.note: Only found in Piura region (very common in Sullana). Usually you won’t be able to see all the 8 digits (0000-0000). In Sullana sometimes you can find it with only 7 digits (000-0000)

metas.name: Pole 8 Digits Vertical
metas.note: 8 digits vertical pole markings are found in La Libertad region (rarely Cajamarca, Ancash)

metas.name: Pole 9 Digits Vertical
metas.note: 9 digits vertical pole markings are rare but can be found in Lambayeque (sometimes Ancash). Sometimes there are two letters instead of the first two digits.

metas.name: Pole Arequipa
metas.note: Red on white / blue on white digits vertical are common in Arequipa region. Rarely the red on white markings can be found in Lima.

metas.name: Pole Barcode Stickers
metas.note: These stickers are mainly in the regions of Tumbes, Piura, Ica and Lima. Differences: Lima - Big numbers in the middle; Ica - Readable numbers at the bottom; Piura & Tumbes: Very small numbers at the bottom.

metas.name: Pole Black Warning Sign
metas.note: This is the most common style of the warning stickers in the northern half of the country.

metas.name: Pole Callao
metas.note: In Callao you often find a light blue - dark blue painted section at the bottom of the poles.

metas.name: Pole COMOL
metas.note: Most of the COMOL poles are found in Arequipa region (rarely in Cusco).

metas.name: Pole Double Horizontal
metas.note: Very long horizontal Pole markings. Common in Junin, Pasco and Huanuco (sometimes Ayacucho, Huancavelica). Typically, the shorter code starts with a 4. The next two letters refer to the region you are in.

metas.name: Pole ENOSA
metas.note: Definitely most common in Piura but Tumbes also has them.

metas.name: Pole ENSA
metas.note: Can be either in the form of a sticker: blue text on white background with black border or in a form of regular marking similar to company name markings. Useful for getting Lambayeque.

metas.name: Pole Horizontal Letters
metas.note: 3 Letters and 3 Digits horizontal pole markings. The letters are an abbreviation for nearby towns (scannable!). Can also be 2 letters, 4 digits. Useful to memorize: CJ - Cajamarca; HI - Trujillo; EN - Chiclayo; CH - Chimbote

metas.name: Pole ICASAC and HHSAC
metas.note: ICASAC are in Ica (rarely Ayacucho) region. HHSAC are in Ica (rarely Huancavelica) region.

metas.name: Pole LDS
metas.note: LDS poles are unique to Lima region.

metas.name: Pole Pucallpa Sticker
metas.note: In the city of Pucallpa you can often find poles with this combination of these four stickers.

metas.name: Pole Rotated Vertical
metas.note: These rotated numbers markings are only found in Apurimac, Cusco and Madre de Dios. In Cusco, you can sometimes find it with other rotated markings.

metas.name: Pole Support
metas.note: Poles with support can be found in the south, most common in Puno, Cusco and Apurimac. Poles without support can be found in the north, most common in Cajamarca.

metas.name: Pole Tacna/Moquegua
metas.note: These blue on white divided markings are only in Tacna and Moquegua regions. Colors can sometimes be inverted as white on blue.

metas.name: Pole White kV Stickers
metas.note: White kV stickers can be found in Lambayeque, Cajamarca (rarely Amazonas) regions. The letters on these stickers may refer to the nearby city’s name. For example: JAE - Jaén.

metas.name: Pole Yellow kV Warning Sign
metas.note: These yellow warning stickers which contain information about voltage (kV) are unique to Ica region and very common.

metas.name: Political Logos Amazonas
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Amazonas.

metas.name: Political Logos Ancash
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Ancash.

metas.name: Political Logos Apurimac
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Apurimac.

metas.name: Political Logos Arequipa
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Arequipa.

metas.name: Political Logos Ayacucho
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Ayacucho.

metas.name: Political Logos Cajamarca
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Cajamarca.

metas.name: Political Logos Cusco
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Cusco.

metas.name: Political Logos Huancavelica
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Huancavelica.

metas.name: Political Logos Huanuco
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Huanuco.

metas.name: Political Logos Ica
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Ica.

metas.name: Political Logos Junin
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Junin.

metas.name: Political Logos La Libertad
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of La Libertad.

metas.name: Political Logos Lima
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Lima.

metas.name: Political Logos Pasco
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Pasco.

metas.name: Political Logos Piura
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Piura.

metas.name: Political Logos Puno
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Puno.

metas.name: Political Logos Tumbes
metas.note: If you see one of these logos you are in the region of Tumbes.

metas.name: Puno 36A Bollard
metas.note: These bollards are unique to road 36A.

metas.name: Puno 38 Thin Road
metas.note: The southern part of Road 38 in Puno, which continues into Tacna region, is the only thin, paved gen 4 road in the region.

metas.name: Puno Divided Road
metas.note: The only divided road in the region connects Puno and Juliaca.

metas.name: Puno Gen 3 Landscape
metas.note: Puno has many gen 3 roads across a flat, high-altitude grass plateau with small hills and few trees. Red brick houses and stone walls are also common.

metas.name: Puno Gen 4 Landscape
metas.note: Puno region is located on a high-elevation mountain plateau (altiplano) and can be recognized by vast grassy plains and rolling hills with sparse vegetation.

metas.name: Puno Juliaca
metas.note: Juliaca is the largest town in the region and is flat, with a lot of red brick architecture. On gen 3 many of the roads inside the city are unpaved.

metas.name: San Martin 105
metas.note: Road 105, northeast of Tarapoto, is a thin paved road north of the mountains, running east-west through the rainforest.

metas.name: San Martin Landscape
metas.note: San Martin region is hilly with lush tropical vegetation, it looks a bit like Colombia. The hills are often not entirely forested but have some grassy patches. If you have random tropical dirt roads with 2024 that are not flat, there’s a good chance you are in this region.

metas.name: San Martin Tarapoto Town
metas.note: Tarapoto is the largest city in the region. It is mostly gen 4 and somewhat hilly. If you are in a large tropical city with visible mountains, it’s likely Tarapoto.

metas.name: Tacna 40
metas.note: Road 40 climbs from Tacna to very high elevations, passing through a variety of landscapes. Parts of the route are unpaved, and you can see several volcanoes along the way.

metas.name: Tacna Bollard
metas.note: This bollard with these reflectors at the top is only found in Tacna region (except for a small spill into Moquegua region on the main highway).

metas.name: Tacna Gen 4 Desert Dirt Roads
metas.note: Tacna region does have some gen 4 desert dirt roads, but they are more common in Ica region.

metas.name: Tacna Olive Trees
metas.note: Olive tree plantations in Peru are found almost exclusively in Tacna region. If you see them you are likely south west of Tacna.

metas.name: Tacna Sand Dunes
metas.note: Tacna is flanked by huge sand dunes on both sides of the city.

metas.name: Tumbes Gen 3 Road
metas.note: The gen 3 roads through central Tumbes are easy to recognize. They are very dry, with sandy soil and a somewhat savanna-like landscape.

metas.name: Tumbes Gen 4
metas.note: Gen 4 roads in Tumbes often have dense, somewhat dry vegetation, including cacti and some palm trees. The landscape can look a bit like northeastern Brazil.

metas.name: Tumbes Main Road Landscape
metas.note: The main road in Tumbes runs parallel to the coast, with ocean to the north. To the south, you often see hills of light-colored, sedimentary soil, which are a good clue for Tumbes region.

metas.name: Ucayali 5N
metas.note: Road 5N from Tingo Maria towards Pucallpa is a very winding, somewhat hilly road with tropical vegetation. It looks similar to the road to Yurimaguas, north of Tarapoto.

metas.name: Ucayali Pucallpa Gen 3
metas.note: The majority of Pucallpa, especially the outskirts, is gen 3. These areas consist mostly of unpaved dirt roads with scattered houses and wooden fences. It looks very rural but is still part of the town.

metas.name: Ucayali Pucallpa Gen 4
metas.note: The center of Pucallpa is gen 4. It is flat and well-paved. Check Pucallpa’s grid to verify. A similar-looking city is Yurimaguas, north of Tarapoto.

metas.name: Ucayali Pucallpa Offroads
metas.note: Side roads off the road to Pucallpa are gen 4, flat, and mostly unpaved.

metas.name: Ucayali Pucallpa Road 18C
metas.note: Road 18C is gen 4, flat, well-paved, and passes through tropical vegetation, sometimes including oil palms.
